text:
Recent work supports separating persistent interests from current intent. [ICSRec (WSDM 2024)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3616855.3635773) learns latent intentions from sliding subsequences using contrastive objectives, without explicit intent labels; its same-target-item alignment remains an assumption about shared intent. [Hierarchical long/short-term modeling (2025)](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y) offers a closer architectural match: dynamic routing builds multiple long-term preference vectors, recent self-attention captures short-term interest, and similarity matching plus time encoding selects relevant historical preferences.

Temporal approaches distinguish recurrence from immediate relevance. [HyperHawkes (WWW 2025)](https://evazangerle.at/publication/peintner-www-2025/) combines clustered latent intents, Hawkes processes for repeated intent, and short-term attention, although its hypergraphs and alternating optimization add complexity. A [September 2026 preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21548) separates historical aggregation from a recent-interest branch modulated by inter-click intervals using distinct state-space encoders. Explicit change-point detection also appears in [SURE, an ICLR 2026 submission](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=htIO088ZZF), but updates recommendation-set calibration thresholds rather than directly routing preference representations.

A lightweight experiment suggested by these findings: retain SASRec, add a recent-window representation and a few pooled historical-interest vectors, then learn a gate from recent/history disagreement and timestamp gaps. Treat a change-point gate as a hypothesis to ablate against ordinary recency weighting; disagreement does not establish changed intent, ownership, or unmet need. Compare against the fixed lexical residual using unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10, with ablations for recent-only, ungated fusion, routing, and temporal gating. The cited results do not establish gains under this pinned protocol.
